clue.text: It's trendy for convict to get out of trial and fine

indicators.note: the convict ends up on the outside of the other pieces, so they sit within his letters

parts.note: LAG is slang for a convict or old jailbird
a test is a trial
fine as in slender or narrow means thin

explanation.surface: A convict hopes to slip out of a trial and a fine, which is apparently the fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get out of' casts the convict as outside the other pieces; 'fine' is the adjective meaning slender, not a penalty.
explanation.definitionFit: The newest fashionable item is what is trendy at the moment; the phrase describes a craze.

clue.text: Wood produces a fire in the chimney

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: lum is a Scottish and northern English word for a chimney
to fire something is to burn it

explanation.surface: Firewood produces a blaze in the chimney.
explanation.definitionFit: Laburnum is a small tree, and its hard wood is used in cabinet-making.

clue.text: Rex wears Hamlet's specially designed clothing

indicators.note: the letters are made into a new design, so rearranged

parts.note: R is short for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A king is dressed in costume made specially for Hamlet.
explanation.definitionFit: Thermals are warm undergarments, a kind of clothing.

clue.text: Locates spectacles, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals the word is judged by how it is said

parts.note: spectacles are sights, things worth seeing

explanation.surface: Someone finds their glasses, apparently by listening.
explanation.definitionFit: To site something is to place or position it, so locates.

clue.text: Water is hot giving discolouration

parts.note: a tarn is a small mountain lake

explanation.surface: Hot water leaves stains on things.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarnish is the dulling film or stain that forms on metal.

clue.text: Anglican in pub getting directions? Holy smoke!

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: an inn is a pub
CE stands for Church of England
S and E are compass directions, south and east

explanation.surface: A churchman asks the way at the pub and exclaims in surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holy smoke!' reads as an exclamation but is a literal definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Incense is burnt in religious services, giving off sacred fumes.

clue.text: Producer needs knowledge and time to meet peak

parts.note: gen is British slang for information or knowledge
an era is a period of time
a tor is a rocky hill or peak, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A film producer needs know-how and time to reach the top.
explanation.definitionFit: A generator is a machine that produces electricity, so it is a producer.

clue.text: Scoundrel caught Bill

parts.note: C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught
an ad, or advertisement, is a bill posted up

explanation.surface: A rogue is finally caught out by the bill he ran up.
explanation.definitionFit: A cad is an old-fashioned word for a dishonourable man, a rotter or scoundrel.

clue.text: Found ecstasy in container

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a crate is a container
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Drugs were discovered in a shipping container.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' looks like the past of find, but it is the verb meaning establish.
explanation.definitionFit: To found an institution is to create or establish it.

clue.text: Pressure has Don going round the bend

indicators.note: one piece goes around the other

parts.note: to don is to put on, or dress
a U-bend is a bend shaped like the letter

explanation.surface: A university don is driven mad by stress.
explanation.definitionFit: Duress is coercion or pressure applied to make someone act.

clue.text: Sovereign tucking into buffet gets bellyache

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other, as if eating into it

parts.note: to buffet is to strike or beat
a sovereign is a pound coin, abbreviated L (from libra)

explanation.surface: A monarch overeats at the buffet and ends up with stomach ache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buffet' and 'bellyache' suggest food, but buffet is the verb meaning strike, and bellyache is the verb meaning moan.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal verbs for complaining or whining at length.

clue.text: Doctor ran to cure storyteller

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with or alter, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor hurried to cure someone who tells tales.
explanation.definitionFit: A raconteur is a person skilled at telling anecdotes, a storyteller.

clue.text: Discharge soldier's duty

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are soldiers; the 's joins them to what follows
a mission is an assigned duty or task

explanation.surface: Being released from service is a soldier's duty.
explanation.definitionFit: Remission is release from a debt, penalty or sentence, a discharge from it.

clue.text: Speaks, when scratching head, of taxes

indicators.note: scratching out the head removes the first letter of the word

parts.note: orates means speaks formally

explanation.surface: Someone speaks about taxes while puzzledly scratching their head.
explanation.definitionFit: Rates were a British local property tax, so rates are taxes.

clue.text: Heartless relative remains free

indicators.note: losing its heart means the central letter of the word goes

parts.note: an uncle is a relative
ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: A cold-hearted family member's remains are set free.
explanation.definitionFit: To unleash is to let loose or set free, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Man met end making revision

indicators.note: the words are used to make something new, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man met his end, which prompted a change to the record.
explanation.definitionFit: An amendment is a change or correction to a text, a revision.

clue.text: Tuck in a sweatshirt

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: An instruction to tuck something into a sweatshirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tuck in' reads as one phrase, but 'Tuck' is the noun meaning food and 'in' signals the hidden letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuck is British school slang for food, and eats is informal for food too.

clue.text: Despatched to find coin in mud

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: despatched means sent
a dime is a US ten-cent coin

explanation.surface: Someone is sent to dig a coin out of the mud.
explanation.definitionFit: Sediment is matter that settles at the bottom of water, such as silt or sludge.

clue.text: Hector accommodates healthy craftsman

indicators.note: one piece makes room for the other inside it

parts.note: to hector is to bully or taunt, to jeer
well means healthy

explanation.surface: Hector takes in a fit artisan as a lodger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hector' looks like a man's name; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A jeweller is a skilled worker who makes gems and precious metal into ornaments.

clue.text: A noble spy

definitions.meaning: a lord such as a duke or earl, a member of the nobility

explanation.surface: An aristocrat working as a secret agent.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer is a titled noble in Britain, and to peer is to look searchingly.

clue.text: Become aware that lies are risky

indicators.note: a risky arrangement is an unsafe one, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Coming to understand that lying is dangerous.
explanation.definitionFit: To realise something is to come to understand or notice it.

clue.text: Get upset in centre of procession

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: the core is the centre

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone becomes upset in the middle of a parade.
explanation.definitionFit: A cortege is a solemn procession, especially at a funeral.

clue.text: Charlie's beaten and rattled

parts.note: Charlie is C in the radio alphabet; the 's means 'is'
lashed means whipped or beaten

explanation.surface: Charlie has been beaten and is shaken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rattled' looks like upset, but here it means made a clattering noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that clashed made a loud metallic noise, which is what rattled ones do.

clue.text: Incentive for a bishop in bed

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
RR stands for Right Reverend, a bishop's title

explanation.surface: A reward for a bishop who stays in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A carrot is an inducement, from dangling a carrot before a donkey.

clue.text: Doctor accepts rebuke when getting a drink

indicators.note: one piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor
a rap is a sharp rebuke

explanation.surface: A doctor takes a telling-off for having a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Grappa is an Italian brandy distilled from grape residue.

clue.text: Bitter cold in desert

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a desert is arid, dry land
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A bitterly cold night in the desert.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrid means sharp and unpleasant in taste or smell, bitter.

clue.text: Water is a barrier to pigs

parts.note: a dam is a barrier across water
swine are pigs

explanation.surface: Some water serves as a barrier to keep pigs in.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam's wine (or Adam's ale) is a humorous old name for plain drinking water.

clue.text: Small border plant

parts.note: an edge is a border

explanation.surface: A little plant for the edge of a flower bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'border' suggests a garden bed, but it simply means edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedge is a grasslike plant growing in wet ground.

clue.text: Help rinse new stock

indicators.note: a new version of the letters means they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Help to rinse the fresh stock.
explanation.definitionFit: To stock up is to refill supplies, which is to replenish them.

clue.text: Glen keeps wife in lodge

indicators.note: one piece holds the other within it

parts.note: a dell is a small wooded valley, like a glen

explanation.surface: Glen keeps his wife living in a hunting lodge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glen' looks like a man's name, but it is the valley; 'lodge' is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To lodge somewhere is to stay or live there, which is to dwell.

clue.text: Have a cup of China in the chateau

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: An invitation to drink from fine porcelain at a French castle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like crockery, but here it is China tea.
explanation.definitionFit: China tea is a variety of the drink, so a cup of China is a drink of it.

clue.text: Nurse keeps Rex, the dog, for arbiter of taste

indicators.note: one piece holds the other within it

parts.note: to nurse is to tend
R is short for Rex, Latin for king
a setter is a breed of dog

explanation.surface: A nurse looks after Rex the dog, who apparently sets the fashions.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who leads fashions is one who decides what counts as good taste.
